newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ascom approaches gearing target in H1.
newsitem.headline: Ascom approaches gearing target in H1.

text.p: Swiss telecommunications group Ascom Holding AG said its gearing -- or debt to equity ratio -- fell to 0.92 in the first half of 1996 from 1.11 at the end of June, 1995, approaching the company's target.
Chief financial officer Jakob Schlapbach told reporters that Ascom's net debt had fallen to 580 million Swiss francs by June 30, from 638 million at end-1995 and 676 million in June, 1995.
During the same period, shareholders' equity rose to 629 million in June, 1996 from 608 million in June, 1995.
Ascom had debt of around one billion francs end-1994.
Schlapbach said Ascom's target set in September, 1995 called for a gearing of between 0.7 and 0.9.
"We are quite close now," Schlapbach said.
One of Ascom's key financial objectives are to improve operating profit, cash flow and reduce its debt load.
"Interest payments are no longer our main problem," Ascom chairman Felix Wittlin said.
Financial expenses in the first half also fell to 16 million francs from 27 million the year before due to higher investment income, but also lower exchange rate losses.
